description.value: The study examined the neural correlates of actively and passively maintaining emotional states using a functional MRI emotional maintenance task.

value: Regions including the dorsal medial frontal cortex, right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and right caudate exhibited greater height and/or width of activation when participants maintained negative emotion than when they did not maintain negative emotion, supporting the active maintenance hypothesis.

### Emotional maintenance task

description.value: Participants viewed positive, negative or neutral pictures and either maintained the emotional state from the first picture to compare with the second picture or rated only the second picture.

spans.text: After viewing the first image of each pair, participants saw either two boxes signifying that they needed to maintain the emotional state from the first image to compare to that of the second image (‘maintain’ trials) or one box signifying that they were to rate their emotional response to only the second image (‘non-maintain’ trials).
